faq.question: Can I find my Android phone if it's switched off?
faq.answer: Not its current location. Find Hub can show the last known location from when the phone was last online, and if offline finding was enabled, nearby Android devices may have reported its location. Once it's off, your best protection is locking it and blocking it through CEIR.

faq.question: How do I find my lost Android phone from another phone?
faq.answer: Open android.com/find in any browser, or the Find Hub app on another Android phone (use guest mode on a friend's device), and sign in with the Google account used on the lost phone. You'll see its location and can ring, lock or erase it.

faq.question: What do I need to block a lost phone on CEIR?
faq.answer: A police complaint or FIR copy, a reissued SIM for your lost number (to receive the OTP), valid ID proof, and ideally the IMEI numbers and purchase invoice. Submit the request on the Sanchar Saathi portal and keep the request ID.

faq.question: Should I erase my phone remotely?
faq.answer: Only if you don't expect to get it back and you're worried about your data. Erasing deletes everything, and Find Hub can't locate the phone afterwards. Lock it first and keep tracking while there's a chance of recovery.

faq.question: Does Find Hub work without a SIM card?
faq.answer: Yes, if the phone has a Wi-Fi connection, or if offline finding is on and other Android devices are nearby. It needs the phone to be signed in to your Google account with Find Hub enabled.
